sentences.text:
Though this matter has come up for admission,
with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken up for hearing.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 18.03.2023 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and C.J.M. and Additional MACT, Bidar, in MVC No.31 of 2022.

3. The injured claimant, aged 58 years, working as cook met with an accident on 03.08.2021, and filed a claim application claiming compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- with NC: 2025:KHC-K:7441 HC-KAR interest.
The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted the compensation of Rs.2,79,349/- with interest at the rate of 9 percent per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant in which it is mainly contended that the Tribunal has granted meagre amounts on all the heads and it is sought to be enhanced.
The Tribunal erred in assessing the income of the claimant as Rs.14,250/- per month and also erred in assessing the disability as 11%.

Hence,
requested for enhancement of the compensation.
4. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for both sides.

sentences.text: 5. Though the petitioner-claimant has stated that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but failed to prove that he was getting the said income.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly taken the notional income of Rs.14,250/- per month and it needs no interference.
He was aged 58 years and the multiplier is 9.

Petitioner examined the doctor as P.W.2 and he stated that petitioner sustained fracture of proximal tibia involving lateral NC: 2025:KHC-K:7441 HC-KAR condyle with implant insitu and partial disability of 34% to the same limb.

6. Learned counsel for the respondent-insurance company argued that P.W.2 in the cross examination has stated that the petitioner-claimant can work in the hotel, and thus it is partial disability not permanent disability.
7. The petitioner has produced wound certificate under Exhibit P7, which shows that he sustained fracture condyle of left tibia and fracture condyle of left proximal is grievous in nature.
The doctor has assessed disability as 34% to the whole body.

Therefore, the Tribunal taken one third of the 34%
as 11%, and awarded Rs.1,69,290/- towards loss of dependency, and the Tribunal also granted Rs.41,559/- towards medical expenses as per the bills produced by the petitioner, and it needs no interference.
8.
The petitioner was admitted in the hospital on 03.08.2021 and discharged on 11.08.2021 and thus, he was hospitalized for a period of 8 days.

Considering his age, occupation and the period of hospitalization, and other relevant NC: 2025:KHC-K:7441 HC-KAR factors, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities, Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
The petitioner might not have attended any other work at least for a period of 4 months.
Thus, he is granted Rs.57,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period.

Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,72,849/- with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.2,79,349/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

9. The award of compensation passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 1,69,290/-
 2. Medical expenses 41,559/-
 3. Pain and Suffering 50,000/-
 4. Loss of amenities 25,000/-
 5. Transportation, extra nourishment 30,000/-
 and attendant charges  6. Loss of earning during the laid up 57,000/-
